title: "Comping rhythm: Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2"
subtitle: "For piano or guitar, built up a step at a time"

This is a lesson on one comping rhythm the [Backing Track](../../tools/backing-track.qmd) band plays: **Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2**. It is built up from 2 simpler patterns, one step at a time, and every step is played by the band and written out as it plays. How the examples work: press ▶ Play, switch players in and out with the buttons beside it, and read what the band will play on the staff underneath: the whole pass is written out when Play starts, before it sounds. The tempo slider at the bottom of the page slows everything down.

[All the accompaniment patterns](index.qmd) · [Comping rhythms](index.qmd#chords)

## The pattern

Sixteen eighth notes over two bars grouped 3+3+3+3+2+2. First bar (shown): 1, the and of 2, 4. Second bar: the and of 1, 3, 4. Beautiful Day.

It belongs in *Straight-eighth rock* and *Dance pop*. Here it is in the straight-eighth rock style with the whole band. Switch the other players off to hear it alone.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2","opts":{"compRhythm":"g333322"}}]'></div>

## Step 1: 3+3+2 (tresillo)

Start with something simpler. Three held chords in a bar of eight eighth notes, grouped 3+3+2: beat 1, the and of 2, beat 4. Clocks, Shape of You, Eye of the Tiger.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-tresillo.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"3+3+2 (tresillo)","opts":{"compRhythm":"tresillo"}}]'></div>

## Step 2: 3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat

The chords play the 3-2 son clave over two bars. First bar (shown): 1, the and of 2, 4. Second bar: 2 and 3. Faith, Desire, I Want Candy.

This is a pattern of its own: [the lesson on it](chords-clave32.qmd) takes it further. Here it is only a step on the way, slowly. The drums keep time with you; switch the others on when it is steady.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Step:" data-choices='[{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

## Step 3: Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2, slowly

Now the pattern itself. Compare it with the step before: press each button while the band plays and watch what changes on the staff.

**How to play it.** Sixteen eighths over two bars grouped 3+3+3+3+2+2. Count the groups, not the beats: one-two-three, one-two-three, ... one-two, one-two. Play a chord on the first of each group.

The band plays it on piano here; the step after next has it on guitar.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="78" data-on="comp drums" data-staves="comp" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Compare:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2","opts":{"compRhythm":"g333322"}},{"label":"3-2 clave / Bo Diddley beat (the step before)","opts":{"compRhythm":"clave32"}}]'></div>

## Step 4: Up to tempo, with the band

The whole band, at 112 beats a minute. Play along, then switch the band's chord player off and take the part yourself.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2","opts":{"compRhythm":"g333322"}}]'></div>

## Step 5: On the guitar

The same rhythm on the guitar. On guitar each chord is a strum or a pluck of a chord shape; a short chord is choked by easing the fretting hand off the strings.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C|Am|F|G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="guitar" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2","opts":{"compRhythm":"g333322"}}]'></div>

## Step 6: Two chords in a bar

Harder: now some bars have two chords, two beats each. The pattern keeps its rhythm and changes chord where the bar does: watch the staff for the hit that lands on beat 3.

<div class="ar-demo" data-style="rock" data-chart="C G|Am F|C G|F G" data-tempo="112" data-on="bass comp drums congas" data-staves="comp bass" data-comp="piano" data-choice-label="Comping rhythm:" data-choices='[{"label":"Groups: 3+3+3+3+2+2","opts":{"compRhythm":"g333322"}}]'></div>

## In other styles

The same comping rhythm in another style it fits. The other players change; yours does not. Notice how the same part sounds different in a different band.
